text:
jamie: Quick async standup — ran into CI failures on the mac M1 runners for the JS SDK quickstart sample. PR #482 passes on linux but mac-latest CI is failing during `npm run prepack`.
alex: I saw that too earlier, failing with a native symbol lookup during a native addon step. Error looks like: `node: symbol lookup error: /.../node_modules/some-ffi/build/Release/ffi.node: undefined symbol: something`
sara: ouch. What I did yesterday: tried a local reproduce on an M1 air (arm64) with node 18 and node 20. Node 18 works, node 20 reproduces the error. Blocker: unsure if we need to pin Node or update the native dep.
mike: quick question — is this happening in CI image `macos-13` or `macos-12`? The workflow uses `macos-latest` which recently moved to 13. Could be an image/toolchain mismatch.
jamie: CI run link: <https://ci.internal.redwood/5221/12|macos job> (devex-bot added the run link)
devex-bot: build #5221 (macos) — failed at step `install` — exit code 127
alex: short-term workaround: add `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-fetch`? (not sure) Longer-term: either pin node-version in the quickstart GH action to 18 or publish a prebuilt binary for arm64 for that native dep.
sara: I'll open two small PRs: (1) docs quickstart note about known M1 node compat and the explicit GH action pin, (2) a CI job tweak to try `setup-node@v4` with `node-version: 18.x` for the mac matrix. Will post PR links here.
jamie: thanks. For the quickstart docs, add a tiny troubleshooting section titled "mac M1 / Node 20" and include the error snippet and the workaround (pin to 18). Users who hit this will appreciate the callout.
mike: today I will: reproduce locally on mac 13 VM, try to recompile the native dep with `npm rebuild --arch=arm64`, and then test the GH action change in a draft PR. Blocker: I need access to the mac CI logs that contain the full linker output — can someone paste the last 30 lines here?
alex: dropping the tail of the log:
```
ld: warning: dylib(/usr/local/lib/libfoo.dylib) was built for newer macOS version (13.0) than being linked (12.0)
Symbol not found: _ffi_cif_maybe
  Referenced from: /Users/runner/work/_temp/.../ffi.node
  Expected in: flat namespace
```
sara: that looks like a macOS SDK mismatch. I'll add a note to the deploy docs to ensure brew libs are installed with the right SDK, and include a `brew install libffi` step in the sample app README if needed.
jamie: aside from CI — what I did today: shipped a small docs cleanup for the SDK quickstarts (formatting and a couple of snippet updates). Blocker: waiting on a quick review from @alex on the code sample changes.
alex: will review PR #480 this morning, ETA 90m. Also I can add a fallback note in the README to run `npm rebuild --update-binary` for arm64.
mike: ping @sara for the docs PRs when ready. We should also add an automated smoke test that runs the quickstart in a node 18 mac matrix job to catch regressions.
sara: yup — adding an entry to the backlog (docs/devex board) for an M1 smoke test. I have the checklist: update README, GH action pin, quick troubleshooting snippet, and link to the CI job.
jamie: last ask — if anyone has a confirmed repro with exact commands that produced the `ffi.node` symbol error, paste it here. I'll include it verbatim in the troubleshooting note.
alex: repro (on M1 darwin, node 20): `git clone ... && cd quickstart-js && npm ci && npm run prepack` — fails during native build. I attached the build log to PR comment.
mike: thanks — I'll try the `npm rebuild --arch=arm64` and report back in this thread.
sara: FYI I filed PRs: docs PR #495 (quickstart M1 note) and CI PR #496 (pin node for mac job). Links: <https://gh.redwood/pr/495|PR495>, <https://gh.redwood/pr/496|PR496>
jamie: perfect. I'll do a short follow-up after we validate CI. :thumbsup:
